definition: A hierarchical control system (HCS) is a form of control system in which a set of devices and governing software is arranged in a hierarchical tree.
details: When the links in the tree are implemented by a computer network, then that hierarchical control system is also a form of networked control system.
story: Picture guardrails on a mountain road — not there to slow you down on the straightaways, but to keep you from flying off the cliff. It is the habit of asking, before every launch, what could go wrong — and then doing something about it. Think of it as the quiet rule that a tool should be useful without being dangerous. It is the difference between “it works” and “it is safe to put in front of people.” That deliberate caution is Hierarchical control system.
